findings.title: [P1] Keep issued tokens out of audit logs
findings.body: Whenever `recordIssuedToken` is called, the raw bearer token is forwarded through `audit` to `console.log`. In deployments that retain or centralize stdout, anyone with log access can replay a still-valid token. Record non-secret metadata or a non-reversible identifier instead.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body: When `returnUrl` originates from a login request, passing it directly to `location.assign` allows absolute or protocol-relative attacker URLs to redirect authenticated users off-site. Validate it as an allowed same-origin path before navigating.

findings.title: [P1] Keep issued tokens out of audit logs
findings.body:
Every call writes the raw authentication token to `console.log`. In environments where console output is retained or accessible to support staff or log collectors, an active token can be replayed to impersonate its owner.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict login redirects to trusted same-origin paths
findings.body:
A caller-controlled value such as `https://attacker.example` or `//attacker.example` now redirects an authenticated user off-site, creating an open redirect usable in login phishing flows.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Apply the anonymous fallback after trimming blank names
findings.body:
For a whitespace-only cached value such as `"   "`, `trim()` returns `""`, but `??` does not treat an empty string as absent. The API therefore returns a blank display name instead of `"Anonymous"`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body:
Every token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is sent to `console.log`. In server deployments, stdout is commonly collected into centralized logs accessible to operators or support systems; anyone with that access can replay a still-valid token and impersonate its holder.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin destinations
findings.body:
`finishLogin` now navigates directly to an unchecked parameter. If `returnUrl` is derived from a query parameter or other attacker-controlled input, values such as `https://attacker.example/phish` or `//attacker.example/phish` create an open redirect immediately after login, enabling trusted-domain phishing flows.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
